chapter.title: Part VI: A practical guide to pstack
chapter.body_html:
Part VI is a practical guide to pstack based on Part 1 and Part 2 of The Complete Guide to pstack, the guide that poteto, the author of pstack, posted on X.

The guide covers "when you use pstack in your own project, where to start and in what order to proceed."

Part VI explains the content of the guide in the following order.

  1. Build a verification skill (Part 1, Chapter 36)
  2. Make the agent understand what the problem is, and have it take over past work (Part 2, Chapter 37)
  3. Design from how users use the product, and try it with prototypes (Part 2, Chapter 38)
  4. Settle the design and turn it into a plan you can carry out (Part 2, Chapter 39)

Part 1 names the verification skill as the first thing the user builds, and covers how to build and use it.

Part 2 covers how the user and the agent decide together what to build, once the verification skill exists. This book organizes the content of Part 2 into 13 key points and explains them across three chapters, Chapter 37 through Chapter 39.

!

Verification skill: a project-specific Skill the agent uses to start and operate the user's app and verify that a change works. For example, if you changed the settings screen, the agent clicks the gear button, opens the settings screen, and saves a screenshot of the changed part as evidence.

The verification skill comes first for one reason. As long as the agent cannot verify its own changes, a person has to check both whether a prototype is any good and whether a plan is done.

In that case, the agent's work cannot move forward until a person finishes checking. The person becomes the bottleneck that stops the work, and spends the day watching the agent.

What you learn in Part VI

After reading Part VI, you will know the following.

  • How to build a verification skill for your own app, and how to keep it up to date as the app changes
  • How to make the agent understand what the problem is the way a person does, and how to have it take over past context
  • How to start design from how users use the product, and how to pick one of several prototype options
  • How to revise the design based on what you learned during implementation, and how to turn it into a plan split into small PRs you can verify

Chapters in this part

Each chapter covers the following.

Chapter What it covers Corresponding guide
Chapter 36: Guide 1: start with a verification skill for your own app Build a verification skill so the agent can verify its own changes Part 1
Chapter 37: Guide 2: share the goal, then align on problem and history Understand the problem Part 2 (key points 1 to 4)
Chapter 38: Guide 2: test a design from how the user will use it Try solutions Part 2 (key points 5 to 8)
Chapter 39: Guide 2: revise the design into an executable plan Settle the solution and turn it into a plan you can carry out Part 2 (key points 9 to 13)

Each chapter builds on the one before it, so I recommend reading in order from Chapter 36.
